name: Kungarakany
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Round, Erich R. 2026. Australian phonemic inventories contributed to PHOIBLE 3.0: Essential explanatory notes. Zenodo record 21471325.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Entry: 'Kungarakany (ggk, kung1259, Phoible inventory 2675) Phonemic inventory inferred from word data in Parish 1983.' — i.e. Parish 1983 has no explicit phoneme chart; PHOIBLE 2675 (contributor Round, source 'Parish nd') is derived from it.

sources.citation: AIATSIS AUSTLANG, entry N14 Kungarakany (Internet Archive copy 2024-12-20 ofhttps://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/N14)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Documentation scores: word list small, text collection medium, grammar 'sketch grammar (<100 pp)' = Parish 1983 (BA Hons, ANU) and Bishop 2000; dictionary = Bishop 2000; manuscripts Evans 1989 pMS 4779 ('Linguistic convergence in the Wogait'), Harvey PMS 5822, Harvey AILEC 0802.

sources.citation: Kungarakan Culture & Education Association / Batchelor Press. 2020. Arrakany tjaput-wudjarmem [Kungarakany insects book], v2.1, 32 pp., linguist Charlee Horni; refs Bishop 2000 and Parish 1983. ISBN 978-1-74131-364-2
sources.note: Nothing. 'Kungarakany Sounds' (pp. 28-29) is a vowel/consonant-to-English key (a, aw, ay, e, ee, i, o, oy, u, uee; b d dj g k l m n ng ny p t tj r rd rl rn rr rt w y) with example words; no word on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2003. Comparative non-Pama-Nyungan and Australian historical linguistics. In N. Evans (ed.), The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia (PL 552), 3-25.
sources.note: Nothing; classification only (Kungarakany placed with Gaagudju in a possible 'Proto Arnhem' grouping).
sources.venue: The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia (PL 552)

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2003. An initial reconstruction of Proto Gunwinyguan phonology. In N. Evans (ed.), The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia (PL 552), 205-268. DOI 10.15144/PL-552.205
sources.note: Nothing on Kungarakany stress. Kungarakany (a c.500-root dictionary) is an outgroup in the etymologies; the only 'stress' passages concern unstressed-vowel reduction in Dalabon.
sources.venue: The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia (PL 552)

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2003. The evolution of object enclitic paradigms in the Eastern Daly language family. In N. Evans (ed.), The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia (PL 552), 185-201. DOI 10.15144/PL-552.185
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives Kungarakany object-enclitic and subject/object prefix tables (Tables 8, 17), citing Evans 1989 (Monash Non-Pama-Nyungan workshop paper) as the Kungarakany source.
sources.venue: The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia (PL 552)

sources.citation: Walsh, Michael. 2002. Transparency versus opacity in Aboriginal placenames. In L. Hercus, F. Hodges & J. Simpson (eds), The Land is a Map, 43-49. Canberra: Pandanus Books / ANU Press.
sources.note: Nothing; mentions a 'Kungarakayn name' of a place near Darwin only.

sources.citation: Lilley, Rozanna. 1987. Paperbark people, paperbark country: gender relations, past and present, amongst the Kungarakany of the Northern Territory. ANU thesis (anthropology). hdl 1885/275607
sources.note: Nothing; no orthography or pronunciation note found (a full-text search for stress/accent orthograph/pronunci/stress/accent); cites Harvey 1986 (Waray MA thesis) for ethnographic points.

sources.citation: Oates, Lynette F. 1975. The 1973 supplement to a revised linguistic survey of Australia, entry 35A* Gungaraganj (AIAS N14). Armidale: Christian Book Centre. (AUSTLANG scan)
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic/classificatory: Tryon's lexical overlap 3.2-15.3% with Daly languages, hence a separate 'Gungaraganyan family'; sources Tryon, Capell, Stanner; 'A full study to expand Tryon's material needed if speakers can be found (it is almost if not quite extinct)'.

sources.citation: Tryon, D.T. 1974. Daly Family Languages, Australia (Pacific Linguistics C-32). Canberra: ANU. hdl 1885/146292
sources.note: Kungarakany is not covered at all (zero hits for any spelling in the whitespace-collapsed text); Tryon had already classified it outside the Daly family. Its 'stress' hits are all grammatical emphasis.

sources.citation: Tryon, D.T. 1968. The Daly River languages: a survey. In E.F. Aguas & D.T. Tryon (eds), Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-14), 21-49. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A14.21
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical survey; Kungarakany is column 23 of the comparative wordlists (pp. 26ff.); no phonology, no mention of stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent the ANU text and extracted text output).
sources.venue: Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-14)

sources.citation: Parish, Lucy. 1983. Some aspects of Kungarakany verb morphology. BA(Hons) (AUSTLANG) / MA (Glottolog, Batchelor Press) thesis, Australian National University. vi+90 pp.

sources.note: The only grammatical description of the language (AUSTLANG's 'sketch grammar'); source of the PHOIBLE inventory; most likely place for any remark on stress, although Round 2026 notes it gives no explicit phoneme chart.

sources.citation: Bishop (Koormundum), Ida M. 2000. Nguñ Koongurrukuñ: Speak Koongurrukuñ. Perth: the author. xxvi+71 pp. (Glottolog 301624 / 557539)

sources.note: The only other 'grammar/dictionary' item AUSTLANG lists; a learner's lexicon with its own pronunciation system whose front matter (26 roman-numbered pages) may contain a pronunciation/stress guide; basis of the Batchelor Institute revival materials.

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 1991. Glottal stop, underspecification, and syllable structures among the Top End languages. Australian Journal of Linguistics 11(1):67-105.

sources.note: Harvey's survey of Top End syllable structure may include Kungarakany (he holds a 500-root Kungarakany dictionary, cf. Harvey 2003) and prosodic remarks; coverage of Kungarakany not verified (T&F page 403).

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 1989. Linguistic convergence in the North Daly: the case of Wadyiginy, Pungu-Pungu and Kungarakany. Paper presented at the Non-Pama-Nyungan Workshop, Monash University, September 1989 (AIATSIS pMS 4779, 'Linguistic convergence in the Wogait').

sources.note: Evans worked with the last speaker (Madeleine England); this is the primary source Harvey 2003 uses for Kungarakany morphology and AUSTLANG quotes for its classification; a convergence study may compare prosody/phonology with Daly neighbours.
